name: Jon Ossoff
incumbencyStatus: incumbent — first term, sworn in January 20, 2021

biography.currentRole: U.S. Senator for Georgia (January 2021 – present); serves on Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI, former chair)
priorRoles: CEO, Insight TWI — investigative documentary media company covering corruption and war crimes (2013–2020)
National security aide, office of U.S. Rep. Hank Johnson (D-GA4) (2007–2012)
Volunteer/intern, office of U.S. Rep. John Lewis (D-GA5) — beginning age 16
biography.education: B.S. Foreign Service, Georgetown University (2009); M.Sc., London School of Economics (2013)
biography.background: Born February 16, 1987, Atlanta, GA. Youngest Democratic senator elected since Joe Biden (1972). Georgia's first Jewish senator. Defeated incumbent Republican Sen. David Perdue in January 5, 2021 runoff, 50.6% to 49.4% (~55,000 vote margin). Characterized as a centrist Democrat by New York Magazine, Washington Post, National Review, and New York Times.
biography.keyBiographicNotes: Inspired by John Lewis biography at age 16; maintained a relationship with Lewis as a formative mentor. Attorney background and documentary filmmaker — investigative journalism orientation evident in Senate oversight work. Only Senate Democrat on the 2026 ballot in a Trump-won state.

statedPositions.quote: Health care guaranteed at an affordable price
statedPositions.notes: Homepage slogan-level language. 2026 campaign is heavily centering ACA premium subsidies — Ossoff states over 1.4 million Georgians could see premiums double if subsidies expire.

statedPositions.quote: More choice increases competition in the health insurance marketplace and lowers costs… forcing private insurers to compete with the public plan on quality and price
statedPositions.date: 2020 (2020 campaign plan — not yet updated for 2026 campaign)
statedPositions.notes: 2020 health care plan document. Publicly stated he does NOT support Medicare for All, but DOES support a public option added to ACA exchange while preserving private insurance. AJC confirmed 'public option' framing in 2020 coverage. No 2026 campaign document explicitly retracts this; his 2026 messaging focuses on ACA subsidies and drug pricing rather than the public option specifically.

statedPositions.quote: Will vote to let Medicare negotiate lower drug prices and to allow Georgians to buy safe and more affordable prescription drugs from Canada
statedPositions.notes: AARP questionnaire response. Consistent with his 2022 vote for the Inflation Reduction Act, which includes Medicare drug price negotiation.

statedPositions.quote: Lower taxes for all but the wealthiest Americans, debt-free public college, and free vocational training
statedPositions.notes: Reconstructed from search snippet of electjon.com platform language.

statedPositions.quote: Massive federal investment in clean energy, grid infrastructure, and research & development
statedPositions.notes: Reconstructed from platform language. Consistent with his Senate legislative record (Solar Manufacturing Act, Clean Energy for All Homes Act, IRA vote).

votingRecord.attendanceRate: High — GovTrack reports Ossoff among most active freshman senators; missed minimal votes 2021–2025

keyVotes.notes: $1.9T COVID relief including expanded ACA subsidies, child tax credit, direct payments

keyVotes.bill: For the People Act / Freedom to Vote Act (2021)
keyVotes.notes: Ossoff introduced the Right to Vote Act (statutory federal voting right) and the Voters' Access to Water Act, both folded into the Freedom to Vote Act. Bill passed Senate committee but failed to overcome Republican filibuster.

keyVotes.bill: John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2021
keyVotes.notes: Would restore and modernize provisions of the original VRA weakened by Shelby County v. Holder (2013)
$1.2T for roads, bridges, broadband, water infrastructure, coastal resilience. Ossoff specifically secured Georgia port and airport upgrades and broadband expansion.
Includes Medicare drug price negotiation, $35 insulin cap for seniors, largest US climate investment in history (~$369B for clean energy), and extension of ACA subsidies
Domestic semiconductor manufacturing investment; Ossoff negotiated provisions for Georgia manufacturers
First major federal gun safety legislation in decades. Enhanced background checks for under-21 buyers, red flag law funding, domestic violence purchasing restrictions.

keyVotes.bill: Federal Prison Oversight Act (signed into law 2024)
keyVotes.notes: Bipartisan bill (co-sponsored with Braun R-IN, Durbin D-IL). Mandates DOJ Inspector General routine inspections of all 122 federal prison facilities; creates new Ombudsman for incarcerated people's rights and safety. Signed into law by President Biden. Followed Ossoff's 10-month bipartisan PSI investigation into corruption and abuse in federal prisons.

One of only a handful of Senate Democrats to vote for this immigration enforcement bill. NRSC criticized him for it anyway. Significant political positioning as the only Senate Democrat in a Trump-won state. Represents a centrist stance on immigration enforcement.

keyVotes.bill: Joint Resolution of Disapproval — Block rifle sales to Israel (November 2024)
keyVotes.notes: Voted to block sale of rifles to Israel (tied to Ben-Gvir's police forces and civilian casualty concerns in Gaza). Voted AGAINST blocking air-to-ground munitions in same batch of resolutions. Nuanced — not blanket opposition to Israel arms.

keyVotes.bill: Joint Resolution of Disapproval — Block $8.8B arms sales to Israel (May 2025)
keyVotes.notes: Reversed course from Nov 2024 position. Said the resolutions 'would have been damaging' to hostage negotiations. AJC noted this as a reversal alongside Warnock.

keyVotes.bill: Joint Resolution of Disapproval — Block assault rifle sales to Israel (July 2025)
keyVotes.notes: Voted to limit automatic assault rifle sales to Israel; voted AGAINST blocking $675M heavy bombs package. Continuing selective/conditional approach.

keyVotes.vote: No — pledged to vote against DHS funding
keyVotes.notes: Joined other Democrats in refusing to support DHS appropriations without civil liberties protections for ICE detainees, following fatal ICE shooting in Minneapolis and publication of his own report documenting 1,000+ abuse incidents in detention.

healthcare.summary: Supports expanding ACA coverage and subsidies; supports a public option competing alongside private insurance; supports Medicare drug price negotiation (voted for IRA 2022); opposes Medicare for All / single-payer; opposes Medicaid/Medicare cuts. 2026 campaign centers heavily on protecting ACA premium subsidies.

climate_energy.summary: Strong pro-climate record (LCV 97% lifetime). Voted for IRA (largest US climate bill). Sponsored Solar Manufacturing Act, Clean Energy for All Homes Act. Supports aggressive clean energy investment. No evidence of fossil-fuel-friendly positions.
sources: Clean Energy for All Homes Act

firearms.summary: Supports universal background checks, red flag laws, and common-sense gun safety measures. Voted for Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022). No NRA grade found — consistent with opposition to NRA priorities.

immigration.summary: Complex centrist position. Voted for Laken Riley Act (enforcement) as one of few Senate Democrats. Led major investigation into ICE detention abuses (1,000+ credible reports). Refused to support DHS funding without civil liberties protections in January 2026. Opposes blanket deportation crackdown; wants reform with accountability.

abortion_reproductive.summary: Pro-choice; opposes restrictions on abortion access; called for federal legislation to protect abortion rights post-Dobbs; SBA Pro-Life America gives him worst grade possible.
sources: Jewish Democratic Council on the Issues

voting_rights_democracy.summary: Strong voting rights advocate. Sponsored Right to Vote Act (first-ever statutory federal voting right), co-sponsored Freedom to Vote Act, John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act. Framed 2026 campaign partly around democracy / opposition to Trump election interference.

justice_prison_reform.summary: Strong prison oversight / accountability record. Led bipartisan 10-month PSI investigation into federal prison abuse; primary sponsor of Federal Prison Oversight Act (signed into law 2024). Also sponsored Civil Rights Cold Case Investigations Support Act. Framing is accountability and oversight — rehabilitation vs. punishment balance unclear but prison conditions focus suggests reformist orientation.

economic.summary: Center-left economic profile. Supports lower taxes except for wealthiest Americans; supported ARP, BIL, IRA (all major public investment). Advocates debt-free public college and free vocational training. Bipartisan on business-friendly measures (small business tax legislation with Hyde-Smith). Introduced Congressional stock trading ban.

housing.summary: No specific zoning or housing supply positions found. Sponsored legislation for HOPE for HOMES Act (energy-efficient home appliances/renovations) but this is energy policy, not housing supply. Housing affordability not a prominent campaign issue based on available evidence.

policing_accountability.summary: Prison oversight work suggests accountability orientation. No specific floor votes on defund/reform policing found. His prison reform record (documenting abuse, establishing oversight) and civil rights legacy framing suggest support for police accountability, but no direct scored votes on policing reform bills found.

evidenceSummary.overallConfidence: high — 5-year Senate record plus extensive 2026 campaign coverage provides strong evidence across most axes
evidenceSummary.notes: Ossoff is unusually well-documented for a first-term senator — his PSI investigations generated significant press, and his status as the lone Democratic Senate incumbent in a Trump-won state has produced extensive AJC and GPB coverage. Main gaps are housing/zoning (never addressed) and policing (relevant votes never came to the floor). His 97% Biden alignment and 6% Heritage Action score confirm a reliably progressive-to-centrist voting pattern; the Laken Riley Act vote and Israel nuances are the most significant deviations from Democratic base positions.
